issues.reason: A finite content clause complementing a noun ('evidence that P') has no licensed carrier — the noun-complement route of *Complements of nouns and adjectives* attaches only surface-PREPOSITION arguments, 'that' is not a preposition, and 'Never coin a relation head' bars inventing one, so this is the coverage gap the reviewer itself lists, not a parse defect.

*Impersonal reported attitudes* registers exactly this limitation — 'a negated conjunct inside such a sealed complement currently has no polarity carrier inside a seal: seal what is expressible and leave the negated conjunct out' — and the parse still projects the definite 'the target' typing at top level as required.

A seal carries one STV over the whole term (*Core patterns*), so no per-conjunct 0.7 is expressible; lowering the wrapper instead would falsely weaken the asserted saying, and dropping (Obligated sk_have_1) would lose more — the parse takes the only licensed option.

An intensifier adverb on a verb has no slot in the vocabulary (Degree is adjective-scoped, Manner is for manner adverbs), and *Quantifiers, generics & scope* sets the precedent to 'leave the unrepresentable adverbial out rather than mis-slot it'.

gaps_confirmed: direct quoted speech ('"...," he said') — sealing under Theme is specified for a finite that-clause complement, not a multi-sentence direct quotation
a negated clause inside a seal has no polarity carrier (registered in *Impersonal reported attitudes*)
a content/appositive 'that'-clause complementing a noun ('evidence ... that they really hate Islam')
a strength-graded status atom (deontic 'should' = 0.7) inside a seal — the seal carries one STV with no per-conjunct carrier
discourse-ordinal 'First,' and the elided ' . . . ' inside a quotation
new_gaps: an intensifier adverb modifying a VERB ('really hate') — Degree is defined for adjectives and Manner for manner adverbs, so emphatic degree on a predicate has no carrier

an evidential/aboutness of-phrase on a non-nominalization noun ('evidence OF the target') — the of-phrase rules cover a nominalization's object and true relational nouns, and only exclude Possession for the 'photo of Mary' case without naming a positive route
notes: Every filed issue is content that the instruction set either explicitly tells the parser to omit (the negated conjunct, the unrepresentable adverbial) or gives no licensed carrier for (the noun's that-clause, a graded TV inside a seal). Nothing emitted is false, ill-typed or over-asserted, so the parse stands as graceful behaviour in gap territory.
